newsitem.title: UK: RALLYING-SCHWARTZ LEADS AFTER KANKKUNEN AND VATANEN RETIRE.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SCHWARTZ LEADS AFTER KANKKUNEN AND VATANEN RETIRE.

text.p: Armin Schwarz of Germany led the British RAC Rally by more than four minutes on Saturday at the end of a first day which saw more fancied rivals crash out.
Among the casualties was Toyota team mate Juha Kankkunen of Finland.

The experienced Schwarz survived where many perished on a day of treacherous conditions through nine timed special stages in northern Britain between the start in Chester and the overnight halt in Leeds.

The rally, not a full world championship event this year, but still regarded as one of the toughest each year, also claimed the ambitions of veteran Finnish favorite Ari Vatanan in a Ford Escort, British hope Alister McRae, in a Formula Two Volkswagen, and another favoured Finn Jarmo Kytolehto in a Ford Escort.
Vatanan, one of three world champions in the event, blew a turbo, hit a log, damaged his suspension and then completed the ice and snow-hit first stage on three wheels before retiring.
Kankkunen and Kytolehto both retired after crashing out in succession at the same corner.

Formula One driver Martin Brundle of Britain also slid off but recovered with the aid of former womens's world champion Lousie Aitken-Walker of Britain. He completed the first leg more than one hour and 40 minutes behind Schwarz.
Veteran Swede Stig Blomqvist in a Skoda was third behind Japan's Masao Kamioak in a Subaru.
